title: 6번: The Dark Side of Desert Solar Farms
fullPassage: It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.
